Today Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now, three hundred and fifty thousand people were watching her stream, and that number was climbing rapidly as the broadcast moved into the Q&A segment.

If the live viewer count hit four hundred thousand, it would be an absolute world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one before her had ever pulled it off. Even the famous and obscenely wealthy Tony Bobbins had only drawn three hundred and ninety thousand in his prime—and that was after decades in the business and with a face the whole world recognized! Now Freya had a chance to smash through that ceiling with room to spare and secure her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought it was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune favors only prepared minds and hands ready to act.

At first, things had just gone reasonably well. A lecture on how to achieve your goals took up an hour. It was the most pleasant part, though only a hundred thousand had tuned in. Expected, yet beneath Freya's level, given her four million followers on Instagram and another twelve million on TikTok. Freya wasn't fond of the latter because it lacked a serious audience, but the algorithms had decreed otherwise.

Another hour was taken up by questions along the lines of "the best age to launch a startup" and "how to get up and start doing," which followers had submitted via a form before the stream. The questions went over well and pushed the live viewership up to two hundred thousand.

Still, that wasn't enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand—a plateau that grew harder and harder to break through each time.

And then Freya went all in, as the New York wheeler-dealers liked to say. Within twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants rigged up a payment form and put out posts on social media. And thus began the surprise segment of the broadcast: open questions for donations. Unmoderated, but on Freya's terms.
